issues.where: d4 (Symptom Progression flowsheet), released at start
issues.problem: This artifact is released at the start of the encounter (release.when = 'start') and already plots the exact overnight jump in swelling (0→3) concurrent with the pain improvement — the key diagnostic pattern the student is supposed to elicit and recognize. Releasing this chart before any history-taking or exam hands the student the entire clinical reasoning pattern (decompression into soft tissue spaces) before they do any work. Fix: either withhold this flowsheet until an explicit history-taking action/review, or make it a plain intake note without the pre-plotted pain/swelling pattern so the student has to elicit the timeline themselves through questions (f2, f3, f4).

issues.where: d5 (Teledentistry Intake Note), released at start
issues.problem: The start-released intake note states the patient 'now improved' tooth pain alongside new overnight jaw swelling, essentially pre-packaging the clinically significant 'pain improved then swelling developed' pattern (the central red flag) before the learner asks anything. This should be trimmed to a more neutral chief-complaint statement without pre-interpreting the significance of the pain/swelling relationship.

This is listed as an 'exam' action performed via patient self-measurement with fingers over video, which is a reasonable telehealth proxy, but it duplicates a2's note about trismus and a11's self-palpation; the role scope says 'inspects by camera' — self-measured interincisal opening by patient fingers is a soft proxy. This is acceptable for telehealth but should be flagged as patient-reported/estimated in both the action name and result (it already is), so this is only a minor consistency issue, not a major scope violation.

issues.where: a6 and f8 vs a12/a13 and m1
issues.problem: a6 and f8 both state the patient denies breathing difficulty and no stridor/accessory muscle use is observed, yet a12 and a13 immediately escalate to 'significant and time-sensitive' airway compromise and mandatory ED referral. This is intentional per the case's teaching point (m1), but the magnitude of urgency assigned in a13 ('immediate ED, not appropriate to do outpatient prescribing') should be double-checked against the fact that there is no stridor and respiratory rate appears normal — this is clinically defensible given the other red flags (trismus, muffled voice, dysphagia, inability to lie flat), so the plan is correct, but faculty reviewers may want the rationale in a12 to explicitly reference the absence of overt respiratory distress as part of 'early' Ludwig's rather than frank airway obstruction, to avoid implying contradictory signals are an error rather than the intended teaching point.

chartAtStart problem list says periapical radiolucency 'per imaging 14 months ago, untreated' which matches a7/d1, but a7's action result is gated behind the student reviewing imaging (action a7), while chartAtStart already discloses the existence and age of this radiograph and its abnormal finding before the student requests it. This substantially reduces the value of a7 as a discoverable action since the key finding is already summarized in the start-of-encounter chart.

revised: a3: clarified name/result to explicitly flag this as a patient-reported/estimated measurement, not a clinician-verified exam finding (reviewer issue 3 - minor consistency fix).

a12: revised rationale to explicitly note the absence of stridor/accessory muscle use and normal apparent respiratory rate as consistent with *early* Ludwig's angina, framing urgency as based on trajectory/red-flag constellation rather than contradicting a6/f8 (reviewer issue 4).

d4: changed release trigger from 'start' to an action-gated release tied to history-taking (a new history-taking/timeline-eliciting action, ref updated to a_history_timeline placeholder -- see note below) so the pre-plotted pain-improves/swelling-spikes pattern is not handed to the student before they take a history (reviewer issue 1).

d5: removed the pre-interpreted framing ('now improved' tooth pain juxtaposed with 'new overnight jaw swelling') and replaced with a neutral chief-complaint statement that does not pre-package the pain-improvement-then-swelling pattern (reviewer issue 2).

NOTE: d4's release.ref was updated to point to a history-taking action; because no existing action currently serves as an explicit 'take symptom timeline history' action, the intended fix requires either reusing an existing history action id in place of the placeholder or adding one -- flagging for case owner to confirm which action id should gate this artifact's release (ideally the action where the learner specifically asks about pain/swelling timeline, corresponding to eliciting f2/f3/f4).
